dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts the Department of Homeland Security, Department of Justice, FBI, and National Counterterrorism Center by mandating joint reporting procedures.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Attorney General, the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and, as appropriate, the head of the National Counterterrorism Center

dimensions.assessment: Requires administrative and reporting duties following completed investigations of acts of terrorism, without altering criminal penalties or substantive enforcement authorities.
dimensions.evidence: submit to the appropriate congressional committees... an unclassified report

dimensions.assessment: Does not specify any federal funding authorizations or direct appropriations for carrying out the reports.
Imposes a new statutory reporting requirement on specified federal agencies concerning acts of terrorism.
dimensions.evidence: Whenever an act of terrorism occurs in the United States, the Secretary of Homeland Security... shall submit

dimensions.assessment: Establishes reporting duties that operate for a temporary period before terminating five years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall terminate on the date that is 5 years after the date of the enactment of this Act.

importance_detail.rationale: The REPORT Act requires specific federal agencies to produce joint unclassified reports and website publications regarding domestic and international acts of terrorism occurring in the United States.
